case.background: You have a long grooved plane, round balls, and a water clock. Collected water mass is a repeatable proxy for descent time. Determine how descent depends on distance, inclination, and mass.
initial_observations: A ball speeds up as it descends rather than moving uniformly.
A shallow plane makes the motion slow enough to compare with a water clock.

controls.description: Distance the ball travels along the marked groove.
controls.name: distance_m

controls.description: Angle of the grooved plane above the horizontal.
controls.name: incline_angle_deg

controls.description: Mass of a geometrically similar round ball.
controls.name: ball_mass_kg

instruments.description: A grooved plane, round balls, a steady water clock, and a balance.
instruments.name: inclined_plane_water_clock

notes: Treat the water flow as steady during the allowed experiments.
Release every ball from rest without a push; each ball rolls without slipping.
The balls are geometrically similar, so their dimensionless rotational-inertia ratio is fixed.
Air drag, rolling resistance, and irregular-ball effects are outside this world.

FinalSubmission.model must equal 'inclined_plane_power_law'. FinalSubmission.parameters must contain exactly reference_water_mass_g, distance_exponent, sine_angle_exponent, mass_exponent. Candidate law: W = reference_water_mass_g * (distance_m / 1 m)^distance_exponent * (sin(incline_angle_deg)/sin(5 deg))^sine_angle_exponent * (ball_mass_kg/0.20 kg)^mass_exponent.

readouts.description: Water collected during one descent; its mass is proportional to elapsed time.
readouts.name: collected_water_g
